A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
tumor infiltrating lymphocyte-mediated immunity varies in different tumors.

the tumor infiltrating immune cells in invasive micropappillary carcinoma are less cytotoxic than those in medullary carcinomas, and this difference is associated with the biological behavior and clinical outcome of these two tumors.

the tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) of medullary breast cancer are more likely to kill cancer cells by Fas/FasL-mediated apoptosis, whereas TILs of invasive micropillary carcinoma are more likely to be cytotoxic T cells that kill cancer cells by perforin/granzyme-mediated cytolysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tumor infiltrating immune cells in the two types are different and the tumor infiltrating T lymphocytes in medulla cancer can kill cancer cells by Fas-FasL pathway.
the tumor infiltrating immune system is not a uniform response to cancer and may actually be a double-edged sword.
tumor infiltrating lymphocyte density and phenotype may be important prognostic indicators in invasive micropillary carcinoma.
